# AUDIT.md: the filter and the reject audit (Chapter 7)
**Anisha Gaikar · JS3 · 2026-11-25.** All numbers are regenerated by `python3 -m js3.report` → `out/report_original.md` (my 76 verdicts as frozen) and `out/report_corrected.md` (with my 5 re-judged items, once they exist).

## 1. What the filter ran on
- **Collection:** live, 14:11 ET on 2026-11-25, `python3 -m js3.collect` (`logs/10`). **5 of 5 boards ok:** Klaviyo 124, Datadog 390, Stripe 772, Lyft 143, Palantir 305, so **1,734 postings** with full text. `data/corpus.jsonl.gz` has its hash in `CORPUS.sha256`.
- **Filter v1.0** (FILTER.md, gated in commit `7ee4178` before any code): **11 kept, 1,723 rejected**, 0 "cannot tell" (no posting was missing its title or text) (`logs/11`, `out/decisions_v1.0.jsonl`).
- **How often each rule failed** (a posting can fail several): R1 title 1,654 · R3 skills 1,554 · R4 years 1,011 · R2 seniority 703.

## 2. How I drew and judged the sample
- **The draw:** the seed (`audit/SEED` = 7375) and the draw script (`tools/draw_sets.py`) were **committed before any judging** (commit `0810190`).
  - **A:** 30 random rejects.
  - **B:** 10 closest calls (rejected, exactly one rule failed, score 4–6, nearest to the threshold of 5 first).
  - **C:** 6 random kept (of the 11).
  - **H:** a held-out 30 (the other 5 kept, 13 rejects with an analyst title, 12 other rejects) for WHAT_MOVES_THE_SCORE.md.
- **The sheet:** all **76** were shuffled into one **blind sheet** (`audit/sheet_order.json`). `python3 -m js3.judge` showed each posting (title, company, location, the requirements part of the text, full text on request) **without** the filter's verdict or the group.
- **The judging:**
  - I judged all 76 myself, 14:27–14:51, against my rule in `audit/AUDIT_RULE.md`, written before judging: "is this posting worth Nadia's time?", answered y / n / ?.
  - Every answer has a reason. Every y/n decision is mine; another Claude chat helped me **word** most of the reasons (SOURCES.md). My verdicts were frozen by hash (`labels/hand_verdicts.sha256`, commit `474e2d5`) **before** I compared them with anything.
- **Copy slips:** 5 reasons were copy-paste slips. Items 7, 8, 22 and 23 carry the reason of a neighbouring posting, and item 65 is a placeholder. I re-judged those 5 in a separate file (`labels/hand_corrections.jsonl`, `python3 -m js3.judge --redo 7,8,22,23,65`). Both versions are reported. The originals were never edited.
- **Other problems in my reasons, disclosed:** five reasons (items 3, 9, 29, 31, 74) and the corrected item 65 lost their **first letter** ("nalyst", "ales", "raud", "taff", "olutions", "pplied"): a keystroke at the reason prompt didn't register. Item 12 said "needs X+ yrs" (a placeholder); I re-judged it at 16:07 (same verdict, n; reason now "analytics lead, senior 'Lead' role, years not stated; Toronto"). In the re-judge I left item 7's reason **empty**. None of these changes a verdict.
- **Speed:** 76 verdicts in 24 minutes (median 15 s per posting, shortest gap 3 s). Most were non-analyst titles decided from the title alone.
- **My judging rule didn't mention location.** `audit/AUDIT_RULE.md` asks "worth Nadia's time" and lists role, tools and years, but **not location**. While judging I also rejected postings for being outside the US and for internship graduation windows. That's a criterion I applied that I hadn't written down beforehand, and it's the basis for R5 (FILTER.md §5). The rule would have been better if it had named location up front.
- **Result of the re-judge (15:39–15:41):** all 5 verdicts came out the same as the originals (5 × n). Only the reasons changed, now written for the right posting (except item 7, left blank). Every number in this folder is the same under the original and the corrected verdicts (`out/report_original.md` = `out/report_corrected.md` in every table).

## 3. Results: how many the filter got wrong
"Wrong" means my verdict disagrees with the filter: a **reject I marked y**, or a **keep I marked n**. Intervals are **Wilson 95% on this sample**.

| Group | Judged | Filter wrong | On this sample | Wilson 95% |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A**: random rejects | 30 | **0** | 0% | **0% – 11.4%** |
| **B**: closest calls | 10 | **1** (*Compensation Specialist*, rejected by R1; my verdict was y) | 10% | 1.8% – 40.4% |
| **C**: kept sample | 6 | **6** | 100% | 61.0% – 100% |
| All 11 kept (C + the 5 kept in H) | 11 of 11, so a **census** of v1.0's keeps, not a sample | **10** (only *Operations Insights, Business Partner Analyst* was y) | — | — |

## 4. What I can honestly say from samples this size
- **0 wrong out of 30 random rejects does not mean the filter never rejects a good posting.**
  - With 30 draws, a true miss rate anywhere from 0% to about 11% is consistent with seeing 0 (Wilson 95%). The "rule of three" gives a similar 3/30 = 10%.
  - Scaled to all 1,723 rejects, that is **between 0 and about 196 wrongly rejected postings**. That's an **estimate from 30 postings, not a measured count**.
- **The random sample mostly tests easy cases.** My reasons for A were mostly "not analyst" for engineering (7), sales (6), manager (5) and senior (5) roles, plus non-US cities (17 mentions). Random rejects come mostly from the 1,654 non-analyst titles, so A says little about the hard cases near the boundary. That's why B and C exist.
- **The close calls are where the misses are:** 1 of 10, *Compensation Specialist*: an analytics-heavy role whose title has no analyst word. Ten is too few to give a rate (1.8%–40%).
- **The keeps are the real problem, and this one is a count, not an estimate.**
  - I judged every one of v1.0's 11 keeps, and only **1 of 11** was worth Nadia's time.
  - That's the measured result for *this collection on this day*, not a rate for future collections.
  - The filter answers "does this look like an analyst job that names her skills?", not "is this worth her time?"
- **Why the 10 keeps were wrong, from my own reasons:**

| Reason (a posting can have more than one; 10 postings, 14 reasons) | Postings |
|---|---|
| Location outside the US | 5: Toronto ×2, Singapore, Mexico City, Bengaluru |
| Finance / accounting / credit role, not data analysis | 4: FP&A ×2, Credit Risk Operations, Processing Cost |
| Internship eligibility (graduation May 2027 vs. the internship window) | 3: all three intern keeps |
| Experience "exclusive of internships" | 1: Data Analyst, SF |
| Software engineering role | 1 |

**None of these is something v1.0 looks at.**

## 5. False friends: words that matched for the wrong reason
1. **"Analytics" in *Software Engineer, Data Warehouse Analytics*** (R1, the title rule). The role word matched, but the job is software engineering, which needs 4 years of SWE experience (my reason). → **R1b** in v1.1.
2. **"years" in "At least 2 years of university education"** (R4). Years of *study* were read as years of *experience*, so this internship got a "≤3 years: SUPPORTED" label. → v1.1 ignores years followed by education words.
3. **"Excel" in "You excel in diagnostic thinking"** (R3, the skills rule): the verb matched as the tool. This one is on a **held-out** posting, so I recorded it and **did not** fix it (FILTER.md §5). Fixing the filter because of a held-out item would contaminate the measurement.
4. **"Analyst" in *FP&A Analyst*** (R1). It matches the role word, but it's a finance-planning role that wants a finance degree. I considered an FP&A rule and **rejected** it after measuring (FILTER.md §5).

## 6. Rules added, cut and rejected after measuring
They're all recorded in **FILTER.md §5**, with versions, evidence and reasons:
- **Added:** R1b (no `engineer` titles, v1.1), the education-years fix (v1.1), R5 US-only location (v1.2).
- **Rejected:**
  - an FP&A exclusion;
  - `specialist` as a role word (1 more keep from 52 such titles);
  - for now, case-sensitive Excel and reading "(2) years", both found on held-out items.
- **Cut:** none. A gave no evidence that a v1.0 rule rejects good postings.

**On the audit groups themselves** (the data I designed the rules from, so this is **not** evidence they work), C's wrong keeps go 6 → 5 under v1.1 and 6 → 3 under v1.2. The 3 left are the two FP&A roles and *Data Analyst, SF*. The test of whether the rules work is the held-out set (WHAT_MOVES_THE_SCORE.md).

## 7. Every audited posting
Generated in `out/report_original.md` ("Every audited posting"): group, id, title, the filter's decision and failed rules, **my verdict**, **my reason**, and whether the filter was wrong. My raw verdicts, with timestamps, are in `labels/hand_verdicts.jsonl`.
